title: Update: Market Chatter: Microsoft Agrees to Keep Shareholder Proposal Rights Through 2027
detail:
PREMIUM
Update: Market Chatter: Microsoft Agrees to Keep Shareholder Proposal Rights Through 2027
MT Newswires
Wed, September 23, 2026 at 12:40 PM MDT 1 min read
MSFT
Trade MSFT on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

(Updates with Microsoft's response to a request for comment in the fifth paragraph.)

Microsoft (MSFT) will maintain current eligibility thresholds for shareholder proposals through next year's annual meeting under an agreement with activist investor Paul Chesser, Reuters reported, citing a copy of the agreement.

The agreement was reached amid proposed changes being considered by the US Securities and Exchange Commission to the shareholder proposal process, according to the report.

Chesser, a director at the National Legal and Policy Center, told Reuters the agreement could give smaller investors an opportunity to have their proposals considered.

Microsoft said in an emailed statement to Reuters that the one-year agreement provides a "clear and predictable process" while the SEC reviews its rules.

"With the Securities and Exchange Commission announcing that its shareholder proposal regulatory framework is under review, we agreed to maintain the current eligibility thresholds for one year, providing Microsoft and its shareholders a clear and predictable process for the next proxy cycle", a Microsoft spokesperson told MT Newswires.

Meta surged 37% over the past month against Alphabet's 1% decline, suggesting a sustained positioning shift toward Meta as AI winner, not one-session noise.

Big Tech is splitting along a single axis in Wednesday afternoon trading. Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) stock is falling several times faster than the technology sector itself, while Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) stock climbs and Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) stock sits essentially unchanged. The sector itself isn't cracking, which points the story at a single name rather than a broad risk event.

JHVEPhoto / iStock Editorial via Getty Images

The Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (NYSEARCA:XLK) is down 0.9% in Wednesday morning trading, and the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) is down 1.12%. Neither fund is collapsing, and Microsoft has barely budged, so what's happening to Alphabet stock isn't happening to technology as a group. That framing puts the burden of explanation on Alphabet itself.

Alphabet stock is at $337.82, down 4% in Wednesday morning trading. Meta Platforms stock is at $754.45, up 2% on the same session, while Microsoft stock is at $498.32, up 0.1%.

Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) settled at $498 on September 22, 2026, down 0.72% on a session when the Nasdaq-100 proxy QQQ closed up 0.81% at a record. The $500 handle keeps slipping through the stock's fingers.

MicroStockHub / iStock via Getty Images

Microsoft is up 3.63% year to date and down 2.4% over one year, while QQQ has returned 21.67% and 24.12% over the same windows. The largest enterprise software company on earth is anchoring an index that keeps making new highs without it. Fundamentals don't explain that gap.

MSFT Price Target — 24/7 Wall St.
Immediate News Is Smaller Than It Sounds

Reports this month describe another round of Microsoft job cuts reaching beyond gaming into cloud, AI, marketing, and research, along with a decision to move development of the next Halo title to Activision studios inside the company.

Put in context, this continues a gaming restructuring first announced in July that targets roughly a fifth of the division and is most of the way through. At a company doing $331.84 billion in annual revenue, a few hundred roles is housekeeping. It is not why the bid disappeared.

Three Real Pressures on the Multiple

Start with rates. The ten-year Treasury sits at 4.96%, near a 19-year high, and the Federal Reserve raised the funds rate to 4.00%, its first hike since 2023. Long-duration megacaps carry the most present-value pain when the discount rate lifts.

Second, the cost argument. An August note from a major bank warned that hyperscaler AI capital spending is outrunning AI revenue, and Microsoft's capex line is the exhibit prosecutors keep pointing to.
